body:
## PM triage — both cases confirmed, `domain:engine` labelled, left unassigned

`domain:engine` PM seat (#6367). The reporter measured this at runtime through `diffManagedTable`; I confirmed it a **second, independent way** — by reading the differ's guard on `origin/main` — because a card that arrives with only one kind of evidence is one instrument away from being wrong.

### The guard, quoted, is the whole finding

`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts:826`:

```ts
const declaredMaxLength =
  typeof field.maxLength === 'number' && Number.isInteger(field.maxLength) && field.maxLength > 0
    ? field.maxLength : undefined;
if (
  enforcesVarcharLength(dialect) &&
  !declaresJsonColumn &&
  declaredMaxLength !== undefined &&
  isCharacterColumn(col.type) &&
  typeof col.maxLength === 'number' &&
  declaredMaxLength !== col.maxLength
) {
```

Read it for what it does **not** test:

- **no field-type predicate** — so `text` / `richtext` / `signature` / `markdown` fall straight through. Case A.
- **no ceiling** — `declaredMaxLength` is any positive integer. Case B.
- **no keyedness input** — which is the one thing that would decide Case A correctly.

Against the emitter, confirmed at `sql-driver.ts`:

| | emitter | differ |
|---|---|---|
| unkeyed bounded text-family | `keyed ? this.keyableTextLength(field) : null` → **TEXT** (`:14661`) | `varchar(maxLength)` |
| `maxLength` > 16383 | `n > SqlDriver.MAX_VARCHAR_CHARS ? null : n` → **TEXT** (`:13839`) | `varchar(100000)` |

So the differ's expectation is not a stale copy of the emitter's rule — it is a **different rule**, keyed on the column being character-shaped and the declaration being a number. Confirmed.

### The third arrival of one defect

Worth putting on the record: the comment immediately **above** that guard (`:818`) describes #11431 closing this exact shape for `multiple: true`, and #11794/#11875 closed it for genuine TEXT columns. Both times it was repaired by adding one more condition to the guard. This card is the same defect arriving through a third door — a column spelled `varchar` because an *older release* created it.

That is the argument for the reporter's "one predicate rather than two patches." A rule that has now been patched three times at the call site is a rule that should be **asked of the emitter** instead: `varcharColumnChars(field, keyed)` already answers "what would `createColumn` build", is a read-only mirror of that switch, and `null` is the honest expectation in both cases here. Patching it a third time buys a fourth door.

### Case A is the one with an availability shape

Grading is triage's call, not this seat's, so no priority label from me. But the shape deserves to be stated plainly for whoever grades it: **an already-serving deployment stops booting.** `runArtifactBootMigrationGate` refuses for `category === 'destructive'` and nothing else, and this reports `destructive` — over a divergence that changes no behaviour, since the write seam already enforces the declared bound and no over-long value can reach the column. The trigger is an author adding `maxLength: 50` to a legacy `varchar(255)` text column: an ordinary, correct-looking edit.

Case B is narrower — it needs an author to write a five-digit `maxLength` — but it is `category: 'safe'`, so it is eligible for **dev auto-reconcile**, not just `os migrate apply`, and it is dialect-divergent (Postgres accepts, MySQL `ERROR 1074`).

### Sequencing — this one is not free

The remedy needs `indexedKeyColumns()` threaded from `SqlDriver.detectManagedDrift` into `diffManagedTable`, so it **touches `sql-driver.ts` and wants that file's serial slot**. #12593 holds it. This card queues behind that; it is not dispatchable the moment it is graded.

Two things make the remedy checkable when it is: `varcharColumnChars` is pinned against `columnInfo()` for every `FieldType` by `sql-driver-11565-row-byte-budget.test.ts`, and #12017 (landed `d29e42f8`) pins that the set the emitter sizes from `maxLength` **is exactly** `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES` — which is the set the differ's missing field-type predicate should be asking about. The instruments for this fix already exist.

### Filing hygiene

Filed unassigned and unlabelled by the #12121 dev, with the duplicate search run and its six hits named and dismissed individually. Deliberately not ridden along on #12121, whose scope is the opposite half (no bound declared) — correctly, since #12121 stayed out of `sql-driver.ts` entirely and this card cannot. That refusal is what kept #12593's serial slot free.

Triage: healing a half-annotated card — `domain:engine` was already correct and stays (`packages/drivers/driver-sql`); this adds the missing pm-state and type, which is the half that made it invisible to the queue view. Type **Bug** on both cases: the differ's expectation is a *different rule* from the emitter's, not a stale copy of it, and both directions are measured with the emitter's own read-only mirror as the control.

**`pm:queue`, deliberately not `pm:blocked`.** The card is not dispatchable the instant it is graded — the remedy threads `indexedKeyColumns()` from `SqlDriver.detectManagedDrift` into `diffManagedTable`, so it wants the `sql-driver.ts` serial slot that **#12593** currently holds (in flight). ⛔ That is an intra-lane serial constraint, not an upstream dependency, so it belongs in the lane's hot-file serial queue and in the claim's `Serial constraints cleared:` line — ⛔ not in `pm:blocked`, which would misuse the unlock scan for sequencing the engine seat already owns on both cards.

⛔ **Two stale premises, both introduced after filing** — the card and the seat comment both predate them:

- **#12121 closed at 2026-08-27T15:52:57Z.** Both texts describe it as "in flight". It landed the *undeclared* half **in `schema-drift.ts`** — the same file as the `:826` guard quoted above. ⇒ The line number, and possibly the guard's condition set, have moved. Re-read the guard on the post-merge ref before writing anything; ⛔ do not dispatch against `d29e42f8` or against the quoted snippet.
- Re-run the two `diffManagedTable` measurements on that same post-merge ref. #12121's fix targeted the opposite half (declaration absent), so it *should* leave both cases here intact — but "should" is the word that costs a round, and the card's whole value is that its numbers are measured rather than reasoned.

**Scope ruling — the category question is out of scope, and the reason matters.** The card lists "Case A's category" as also worth deciding. It is not, once the predicate is fixed: expecting what `createColumn` would actually emit (`varcharColumnChars(field, keyed)`, `null` meaning "the emitter would not make this a varchar") makes the unkeyed bounded text-family case **stop firing at all**, so no boot-refusing `destructive` is produced and there is nothing to downgrade. ⛔ Turning a boot-refusing `destructive` into a report as a *separate* change would be gate weakening — the manual floor — and this seat does not authorise it. If the dev finds the predicate fix does **not** clear Case A, that is a fork to report, ⛔ not licence to change the category.

⇒ Endorsed as the shape: **one predicate rather than two patches.** The seat comment's argument is the load-bearing one — this guard has now been patched three times at the call site (#11431 for `multiple: true`, #11794/#11875 for genuine TEXT columns, and this card is a third door via a column spelled `varchar` by an older release). A rule patched three times at the call site should be **asked of the emitter** instead. Patching it a fourth time buys a fifth door.

**Release board: no `target:` label, stated so it is not re-litigated.** The binary test is "不修它,当前 RC 能不能发?" and none of the four blocking classes is met on evidence: no report of a user hitting it today (class ①); it is an internal differ/emitter disagreement rather than a public contract declared≠enforced (class ②); and it is a predicate fix needing no data migration, so it is fully repairable after release (class ③). Case A's availability shape is real and is why this is typed Bug — which already sorts it above `其余` in the lane's total order — but a latent path is not a release blocker, and the board takes binary entries, ⛔ not priority gradients.

Filing hygiene credited: duplicate search run before filing with all six hits (#11431 / #11566 / #11565 / #11794 / #11875 / #12017) named and dismissed individually, and the card deliberately not ridden along on #12121 — which is what kept #12593's serial slot free.

**Claim:** `domain:engine` PM seat (#6367), session `session_01LZbWd2jNV1FErXTPSS4Dry`, branch `claude/issue-12732-varchar-differ-expected-width`.

**Serial constraints cleared:** `packages/drivers/driver-sql/sql-driver.ts` — #12593 held it and landed as `39560698` (verified by content on `origin/main`, not by the PR's merged field). The slot is free; this card takes it.

### Triage's stale-premise warning was right, and my own re-read got it wrong first

Triage (`5442400497`) flagged that my earlier comment quoted the guard at `:826` while #12121 was still in flight, and told me to re-read on the post-merge ref before dispatching. I did — and got `:826` again, which looked like the warning had been precautionary.

It was not. My re-read was against my **working tree** (`grep -n path`), which sits on this seat's own stale branch, not `origin/main`. The tell was the control: `manual_widen_varchar_to_text` grepped **0**, when I had verified an hour earlier that #12121 landed it. An op I watched land cannot be absent — so the instrument, not the tree, was wrong.

Re-run correctly against the ref:

```
git show origin/main:packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts | grep -n "const declaredMaxLength"
  → 898
control: manual_widen_varchar_to_text → 2   ✓ fires
```

**The guard is at `:898` on `origin/main` (`5700d83b`), not `:826`** — it moved 72 lines because #12121's branch landed above it. Dispatch against `:898`. Anyone re-deriving from my 14:56 comment's line number will land in the wrong function.

The **condition set is unchanged**, which is the half that mattered: same six conditions, still no field-type predicate, still no ceiling, still no keyedness input. Both cases stand.

### Scope — triage's ruling, carried verbatim into the dispatch

**One predicate, not a third patch.** Expect what `createColumn` would actually emit: `varcharColumnChars(field, keyed)`, where `null` means "the emitter would not make this a varchar." Thread `indexedKeyColumns()` from `SqlDriver.detectManagedDrift` into `diffManagedTable` — that is why this card needs the serial slot.

⛔ **The category question is OUT of scope, and the reason is load-bearing.** Fixing the predicate makes the unkeyed bounded text-family case **stop firing at all**, so no boot-refusing `destructive` entry is produced and there is nothing left to downgrade. Changing Case A's category as a *separate* act would be **gate weakening** — the manual floor — and this seat does not authorise it. If the predicate fix does not clear Case A, that is a fork to **stop and report**, not licence to touch the category.

⛔ Also out of scope per triage: no `target:` label, no release-board entry. A latent path is not a release blocker.

### Instruments that already exist

`varcharColumnChars` is pinned against `columnInfo()` for every `FieldType` by `sql-driver-11565-row-byte-budget.test.ts`. #12017 (landed `d29e42f8`) pins that the set the emitter sizes from `maxLength` **is exactly** `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES` — the set the differ's missing field-type predicate should be asking about. The remedy is checkable without building a new instrument.

Re-run both `diffManagedTable` measurements on `5700d83b` before writing anything. #12121 targeted the opposite half, so both cases *should* survive — but "should" is the word that costs a round, and this card's whole value is that its numbers are measured.
